rendered: The sugar-derived microporous carbon spheres were loaded with 35[1] of sulfur, per the paper: wt % sulfur completely confined in the micropores of the[2] carbon spheres. The method was an isothermal vapor phase process[3] in which the carbon powder is infiltrated with sulfur at 175 °C[4], lasting 1 h[5]. The authors contrast this with their earlier work, which reached more than 80[6] wt % sulfur loading without needing micropore confinement.
